formats.key: claimExitedAssets(uint256 positionTicket, uint256 timestamp, uint256 exitQueueIndex)
effects: Sends the ETH from the signer's processed exit request to the signer (msg.sender), in an amount the contract computes from storage.
Deletes the signer's exit request. If part of it is not yet processed, re-creates it under a new position ticket.
formats.shown: Only the intent "Claim exited assets". No asset, amount or recipient is shown, and all three ticket parameters are hidden.

findings.title: claimExitedAssets: the ETH amount claimed comes from storage and cannot be shown from calldata.
findings.evidence: VaultEnterExit.sol claimExitedAssets: `(.., exitedAssets) = calculateExitedAssets(msg.sender, ...)`; `_transferVaultAssets(msg.sender, exitedAssets)`. Case 0: signer receives 0.252190983937536054 ETH and the screen has no fields. The recipient is always msg.sender, which is the signer.
findings.fix: None possible for the amount. The intent can name the asset (see the other finding).

findings.title: claimExitedAssets: the intent says "assets" but never says ETH is paid to the signer's wallet.
findings.evidence: descriptor intent "Claim exited assets". VaultEthStaking._transferVaultAssets: `Address.sendValue(payable(receiver), assets)`. Case 0 reader: "Which asset and how much will be claimed" is listed as unsure.
findings.fix: Use an intent like "Claim unstaked ETH to your wallet".

cases.notes: The signer receives 0.2522 ETH. The screen gives neither the asset nor the amount, and the amount cannot come from calldata. The reader guessed the direction right.

effects: Takes msg.value ETH from the signer into the vault.
Mints vault shares worth that ETH to `receiver`, at the current share price.
`referrer` is only emitted in an event.
formats.shown: Stake ETH, with the shares receiver and the ETH amount (msg.value).

findings.title: deposit: the receiver addressName types (eoa, wallet) are narrower than the code allows.
findings.evidence: descriptor `#.receiver` params.types ["eoa","wallet"]. VaultEnterExit._deposit only checks `to != address(0)`, so any contract can receive the shares.
findings.fix: Drop the types restriction or add "contract".

findings.title: deposit: the number of shares minted depends on the share price in storage and is not shown.
findings.fix: None. A descriptor cannot show it.

cases.notes: 149 ETH out, shown as "149 ETH". The shares receiver is the signer.

effects: Removes `shares` of vault shares from the signer's balance into the exit queue (no token transfer).
Creates an exit request keyed to `receiver`. Only `receiver` can later claim the ETH it yields.
If the vault is not collateralized, the code instead burns the shares and sends the ETH to `receiver` at once.
Reverts if this breaks the signer's osToken position LTV.
formats.shown: Enter exit queue, with the share count as a raw integer and a receiver address.

findings.title: enterExitQueue: shares are shown as a raw 18-decimal integer.
findings.evidence: descriptor `#.shares` format "raw". Case 2 shows "1202830776429082680". The reader had to guess that this is about 1.2028.
findings.fix: Use format "unit" with decimals 18 and base "shares" (or the vault's share symbol).

findings.title: enterExitQueue: the "Receiver" label doesn't say this address gets the right to claim the ETH.
findings.evidence: VaultEnterExit._enterExitQueue: `_exitRequests[keccak256(abi.encode(receiver, block.timestamp, positionTicket))] = shares`. claimExitedAssets pays msg.sender only, so a receiver other than the signer takes the claim.
findings.fix: Label it "ETH receiver (can claim)" and use an interpolated intent such as "Unstake {shares} shares, ETH to {receiver}".

findings.title: enterExitQueue: the receiver addressName types (eoa, wallet) are narrower than the code allows.
findings.evidence: descriptor `#.receiver` types ["eoa","wallet"]. The code only rejects address(0).

cases.notes: The mined tx moved no tokens. The share lock is internal to the vault, and the shown shares and receiver (the signer) match the calldata.

effects: Delegatecalls each `data` entry on the vault itself, as msg.sender = signer. Every inner call has its own effects: claiming ETH, entering the exit queue, minting or burning osToken, and so on.
The function is not payable, so no ETH leaves the signer at this level.
formats.shown: The intent "Multicall", then each inner call rendered with this descriptor's own formats.

findings.title: multicall: the inner claimExitedAssets shows no ETH amount, because the amount comes from storage.
findings.evidence: Case 4: signer receives 1.307498473925919552 ETH. The nested screen is "Claim exited assets" with fields [].
findings.fix: None for the amount. Rename the inner intent to name ETH.

findings.title: multicall: inner calls to signer functions with no format here (mintOsToken, burnOsToken, redeemOsToken) cannot render.
findings.evidence: Multicall.sol: `Address.functionDelegateCall(address(this), data[i])` runs any vault function. descriptor display.formats only covers 5 other functions. EthVault.sol has depositAndMintOsToken and updateStateAndDepositAndMintOsToken.
findings.fix: Add formats for the osToken functions and the other user-callable vault functions.

findings.title: multicall: the intent "Multicall" tells a non-expert nothing.

cases.notes: The signer receives 1.3075 ETH through the inner claim. The reader knew assets would be claimed, but not the asset or the amount.

effects: Harvests the keeper-verified rewards or penalties into the vault's total assets and mints fee shares to the vault's fee recipient.
Processes the exit queue. It moves none of the signer's assets.
formats.shown: Update Vault State, with all harvest parameters hidden.

cases.notes: No movements for the signer, which matches the code.

findings.title: updateStateAndDeposit: the intent "Update & Deposit" does not say ETH is staked, unlike the deposit format.
findings.evidence: descriptor intent "Update & Deposit" vs deposit's "Stake ETH". Case 3 reader: "What 'Update' does exactly" is listed as unsure.
